-# Protocolo V2 — execução e contexto integrados
-
-O padrão para novos lotes é o [fluxo enxuto](fluxo-enxuto.md). Durante seu planejamento e despacho Go, não execute preparação/indexação/process/flow do Node legado nem acrescente gates/auditores/QA. As instruções operacionais Node abaixo só se aplicam ao modo legado explícito; regras de negócio e segurança do projeto permanecem vigentes.
-
-Consulte apenas a seção da próxima ação. `contexto/contexto.mjs --help` lista comandos; os testes em `contexto/tests/` fornecem exemplos executáveis completos. Este protocolo complementa risco, regras locais e proteções de banco; não concede publicação externa.
-
-## Inicialização automática
-
-Requer Node.js >=22.13 com `node:sqlite` e Git no PATH. Não usa npm, API de modelo, embeddings nem cadastro de MCP. A skill chama `scripts/preparar-contexto.mjs --project RAIZ_GIT_REAL`; esse helper chama o Contexto incluído em `_shared/contexto`. Não peça ao usuário `init`, `setup` ou configuração de servidor. Sem runtime/permissão, registre o bloqueio real.
-
-`ensure` registra metadados locais, preserva configuração e prepara o índice. Não instala hooks por padrão, não altera configuração global nem arquivos rastreados. Em main/master, só prepara dados locais; gates, implementação e integração exigem branches de trabalho. `CONTEXTO_CLI` é override explícito opcional; não é necessário.
-
-O primeiro diretório existente da lista abaixo determina o armazenamento, independentemente do cliente que chama a skill:
-
-1. `skills/_shared/.contexto/` na fonte das skills;
-2. `.agents/skills/_shared/.contexto/`;
-3. `.claude/skills/_shared/.contexto/`;
-4. `.agent/skills/_shared/.contexto/`.
-
-Sem esses diretórios, crie apenas o armazenamento em `.agents/skills/_shared/.contexto/`. Uma configuração existente em `RAIZ/.contexto/` continua sendo usada; não migre/copie aprovações silenciosamente. Dois bancos/configurações da mesma raiz são erro, não fontes concorrentes. A preparação devolve `prepared:true`, raiz e caminho absoluto do SQLite. Metadados Git `info/exclude` mantêm os dados locais fora do Git. Cada worktree tem identidade e banco próprios; nunca distribua `.contexto` com as skills.
-
-## Planejamento canônico
-
-Preserve o manifesto Markdown e as convenções do projeto. Gere ao lado dele:
-
-- `planning-context.json`: `schema:1`, `batch_id`, `decisions` (ID, origem, fato/decisão/hipótese, referência), `open_questions`, `specifications` (tarefa e caminho), `contracts` e `dependencies`. Preserve IDs e atualize o mesmo arquivo por lote; não copie documentos inteiros.
-- `lote-<id>.json`: entrada executável para `flow load`. Caminhos são absolutos reais, derivados da máquina atual; Git usa SHAs completos. Não deixe placeholders executáveis.
-
-Formato do manifesto JSON (campos obrigatórios):
-
-```json
-{
-  "schema": 1,
-  "id": "LOTE-1",
-  "tasks": [{
-    "id": "T1", "ticket": "TICKET-1",
-    "repository": "/caminho/real/repo",
-    "root": "/caminho/real/worktrees/t1",
-    "branch": "feature/t1", "base_sha": "SHA_COMPLETO_REAL",
-    "dependencies": [],
-    "definition": {
-      "id": "T1", "profile": "padrao", "risk_level": "R2",
-      "rationale": "Justificativa concreta do comportamento e impacto.",
-      "risk_factors": ["functional"],
-      "criteria": ["AC-01"],
-      "sources": ["docs/especificacao-t1.md"]
-    }
-  }],
-  "integrations": [{
-    "id": "GRUPO-1", "repository": "/caminho/real/repo",
-    "root": "/caminho/real/worktrees/revisao-lote1",
-    "branch": "revisao/lote1", "base_sha": "SHA_COMPLETO_REAL",
-    "members": ["T1"]
-  }]
-}
-```
-
-Este exemplo é um contrato, não um comando pronto. `sources` aponta para arquivos existentes na base; arquivos novos de implementação são cobertos pelo snapshot Git completo. Para especificação canônica externa à camada (por exemplo a pasta de planos central da Intranet), declare `external_sources:[{root:RAIZ_REAL_CONFIRMADA,source:CAMINHO_RELATIVO_POSIX}]` e `spec` como referência. O runtime preserva os hashes dessas fontes no snapshot, sem copiar documentos ou ampliar a indexação. Nesse caso sources pode ser vazio; a árvore Git inteira continua coberta. Não copie nem altere critérios para satisfazer a validação. Cada tarefa pertence a um grupo Git; backend/frontend usam grupos distintos e o mesmo `ticket` para compartilhar os limites de rodadas. `dependencies` são IDs deste lote. A skill valida também contratos entre grupos/repositórios. Plano legado sem classificação explícita continua crítico.
-
-## Coordenador e próxima ação
-
-Na raiz coordenadora preparada, use a CLI embarcada com `--project` explícito:
-
-1. `flow load --file MANIFESTO_JSON`: importa uma definição imutável, validando DAG, bases e grupos; repetir o mesmo manifesto é idempotente.
-2. `flow claim --batch ID --session SESSAO_COORDENADORA`: assume/renova lease de 30 minutos. Mesmo expirado, outro proprietário não é removido automaticamente; confira que parou e use `flow release --batch ID --expected-session SESSAO_ANTIGA` antes de assumir. Não invente morte de processo.
-3. `flow next --batch ID`: devolve ações compactas. Execute as independentes com no máximo duas simultâneas inicialmente; meça antes de aumentar. Não chame IA para escolher transição já devolvida pelo runtime.
-4. `flow prepare --batch ID --task T --session S`: cria worktree em branch final/base fixa, prepara contexto e registra ownership antes da criação. Worktree externa ao lote não é apropriada. Dependências Git aprovadas da mesma camada são incorporadas; a base efetiva do review fica registrada após essa incorporação.
-5. Delegue a ação ao agente nativo do cliente, em sessão independente quando o gate exigir. Antes de delegar, gere `pack --project WORKTREE --task T --role PAPEL --mode initial|focal|integrated --max-bytes 10000`. Papel: implementer/reviewer/auditor/qa/coordinator. Aumente orçamento ou expanda referências se faltar critério essencial; não omita cobertura.
-6. Registre o JSON devolvido pelo executor com `flow event --batch ID --task T --session S --file EVENTO`. O coordenador usa sua raiz; `event.session` identifica a sessão executora. Dentro de lote, não mantenha estado Markdown paralelo nem use eventos avulsos como segunda coordenação. Consulte `flow next` após cada resultado.
-
-A CLI não inicia modelos por assinatura/API e não cria sessões independentes por conta própria. O cliente que executa a skill faz a delegação; ausência dessa capacidade bloqueia o gate independente. O runtime reduz decisões operacionais da sessão coordenadora, mas não promete execução autônoma com o cliente fechado.
-
-## Eventos, evidência e correção
-
-Todo evento contém `id`, `task`, `session`, `expected_revision` e `type`. Em `type:gate`, informe `gate`, `status`, `snapshot` atual de `snapshot --task T`, e `evidence:[{source,detail}]`; os hashes são calculados e preservados pelo runtime. Caminhos relativos pertencem à worktree. O relatório deve identificar comandos/cenários, resultado observado, ambiente/isolamento, base/HEAD e limitações.
-
-Gates iniciais: `implementation`, `review`, `audit`, `qa`. Status: PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED, ou NA_SEM_ACHADOS/COBERTO_NO_REVIEW somente nas condições do risco. R3/R4 exigem revisor-de-qa separado. Em R0–R2, QA_COVERAGE registra COBERTO_NO_REVIEW com sessão do revisor independente, coverage completa, checks determinísticos aplicáveis e evidência íntegra. Lacuna/risco sem cobertura exige evento require_qa com reason; o runtime invalida dispensas. Planos persistidos sem risk_level mantêm a política anterior. Review informa findings, finding_ids, coverage e, nos novos R0–R4, finding_details (id, severity P0–P3, file, line, evidence, impact, expected_test). QA informa cobertura e matriz observada. PASS não é consequência automática de leitura de código, contador, booleano ou código de saída de build.
-
-Repositórios Git usam snapshot completo da árvore commitada, base e estado local, incluindo código fora de `sources`. PASS exige árvore limpa. Commits em `docs/historico/reviews/` e `docs/historico/entregas/` não invalidam o código; requisitos, ADRs, configuração, testes e demais docs continuam cobertos. Não guarde executáveis nesses diretórios históricos. Evidência alterada invalida o gate mesmo quando o código não muda. As identidades de sessão são declarações verificadas por diferença, não autenticação criptográfica; o coordenador confere a procedência real dos agentes.
-
-Com achados, use `type:audit_decision`, snapshot, evidências e `decisions:[{id,decision,reason,blocking}]`. APLICAR é registrado **antes** de corrigir. ADIAR/REJEITAR precisam de fundamento; bloqueante confirmado não pode ser adiado/rejeitado. Não marque `verified:true` pelo próprio auditor.
-
-Para corrigir:
-
-1. Registre `type:round`, `kind:technical`, `round_id` estável e único desta rodada. O runtime vincula a rodada ao plano de auditoria pendente. Agrupe APLICAR compatíveis com dependências explícitas; não agrupe apenas para esconder unidades independentes.
-2. Delegue somente os IDs APLICAR ao implementador, com arquivos, origem, negócio e teste esperado. Feche em modo CORRECAO, commit local e nova implementação observada. Não recrie registro/índice por ID.
-3. Devolva ao revisor independente `type:revalidate`, snapshot novo, evidência, `coverage`, `impact_checked:true`, `results:[{id,status:"VERIFICADO"}]` exatamente para os IDs APLICAR. O snapshot de origem inalterado não é aceito. ID ainda presente/regressão exige novo review/auditoria com os IDs pendentes; nunca invente VERIFICADO.
-4. Preserve os pareceres antigos nos eventos. O novo gate registra a revalidação, não reescreve o veredito original nem cria uma nova aprovação do auditor sobre código que ele não examinou.
-
-Até três rodadas técnicas e três de QA por `ticket`, somadas entre camadas e integração. Repetição do mesmo evento/round_id não consome outra; uma rodada antiga não autoriza novas decisões. QA FAIL registra nova rodada `kind:qa` antes de corrigir; faça review técnico focal das alterações e QA observado dos bugs/regressões, mantendo a matriz anterior por referência. Use `flow isolate --batch ID --task T --session S --reason MOTIVO` para bloqueios reais; dependentes são isoladas e independentes continuam. Não contorne falhas editando SQLite.
-
-## Integração, pacote e limpeza
-
-`flow integrate --batch ID --group G --session S` exige membros/dependências aprovados, cria a candidata em `revisao/` e faz merges locais sem force. Conflito preserva a candidata e bloqueia; não resolve ours/theirs, não faz reset/rebase nem altera checkout principal. Se membros mudarem, preserve a candidata antiga e use uma nova candidata pelo protocolo `flow candidate`.
-
-Registre gates finais com `flow receipt --batch ID --session S --file RECIBO`: `id`, `group`, `expected_revision` do lote, `session` executora, `stage` checks/review/audit/qa, `status`, snapshot/hash e `head_sha` atuais de `flow status`, `evidence:[{source,hash}]`. Review/QA exigem `coverage_complete:true`; review PASS exige `findings:0`. Perfil crítico atual do grupo exige auditor independente mesmo sem achados. Auditoria NA é evento determinístico nos demais, com referência ao review sem achados. Novos achados bloqueiam: review FAIL registra findings/finding_ids; a próxima ação AUDIT_INTEGRATED_FINDINGS pede auditor independente. Registre triagem integrada em audit FAIL/BLOCKED com decisões por ID, sem aprovar a candidata. ROUTE_INTEGRATED_CORRECTIONS e CORRECT_INTEGRATED_QA exigem identificar as tarefas responsáveis, auditar/corrigir nelas, revalidar e reconstruir candidata. Não repita review/QA falho sem alteração material.
-
-No review/QA integrado, investigue exclusivamente interações, mudanças de contrato, resoluções de merge e regressões do conjunto. Preserve evidências individuais válidas; não repita toda a análise semântica dos arquivos inalterados. Testes automatizados abrangentes podem continuar rodando.
-
-Em grupos exclusivamente R0–R2 sem QA condicional, INTEGRATED_QA_COVERAGE aceita recibo qa COBERTO_NO_REVIEW da sessão do review, coverage_complete:true, checks e evidências próprias das interações. R3/R4 mantêm QA PASS observado por sessão separada. Mudança da exigência de QA de um membro invalida a candidata anterior, mesmo sem mudança de SHA/perfil. Nunca reaproveite a dispensa antiga depois de elevar o risco.
-
-`flow package --batch ID` gera pacote humano em `generated/` do armazenamento local. Distinga pronta para integrar de validada, limpeza pendente, parcial e bloqueada. Complemente o roteiro funcional/PR com texto da IA somente onde houver conteúdo novo; não publique ClickUp, push ou PR.
-
-Antes de remover uma worktree, encerre os executores e execute `flow cleanup-check --batch ID --task T|--group G --session S`. O script verifica ownership, topologia, branch, operações pendentes, ignorados e links. `node_modules`, junction, arquivo desconhecido ou ignorado único bloqueiam; nunca siga links nem apague recursivamente. Histórico Contexto é arquivado no Git comum. Com recibo seguro e comprovação dos executores parados, execute `flow cleanup ... --executors-stopped yes`. Remoção usa somente Git sem force e preserva branches; retomada não remove de novo.
-
-Após liberar a worktree da candidata, `flow deliver --batch ID --group G --session S` troca somente o checkout principal limpo para a branch aprovada. Se estiver sujo, preserve-o e registre comandos no pacote. Gere o pacote novamente após limpeza/entrega para inventário real e resultado final. Uma tarefa isolada nunca vira concluída por constar no pacote.
-
-## Medição e documentação
-
-Use `capture --project WORKTREE -- EXECUTAVEL ARGUMENTOS` para executar validação permitida e reter código de saída/log saneado. Não é sandbox nem prova de isolamento de banco. Prefira log diagnóstico resumido; leia a captura completa só ao investigar. Nunca execute teste de banco sem prova de isolamento conforme regras locais.
-
-Importe `usage --file JSON` com contadores do cliente; sem telemetria, registre `observed:false` e tokens null. Registre papel, modelo, sessão, tentativa, duração e ferramentas quando disponíveis. `report` separa medições reais de estimativas de bytes; não invente economia nem contador indisponível. O teste comparativo de consumo real exige lotes equivalentes, entregas aprovadas e análise de defeitos/retrabalho.
-
-`delivery --file JSON` gera estrutura/inventário por Git. Modos: ENTREGA_INICIAL, CORRECAO e FECHAMENTO_INTEGRADO. IA fornece título, contexto, motivo, riscos e como testar; o script não chama modelo, não commita, não publica e não acrescenta índice externo. O mesmo implementador usa fechar-entrega; não abra outro agente apenas para copiar metadados. Coordenador serializa a linha do índice após o commit real, usando chave do registro; CORRECAO atualiza o registro existente antes do bloco ClickUp e não cria outra linha.

@@ -1,22 +0,0 @@
-# Contexto automático por worktree
-
-O padrão para novos lotes é o [fluxo enxuto](fluxo-enxuto.md). Durante seu planejamento e despacho Go, não execute preparação/indexação/process/flow do Node legado nem acrescente gates/auditores/QA. As instruções operacionais Node abaixo só se aplicam ao modo legado explícito; regras de negócio e segurança do projeto permanecem vigentes.
-
-O código Contexto está em `_shared/contexto/`. Não depende de instalação externa ou cadastro de MCP. O usuário não executa init por worktree. Siga o [protocolo V2](protocolo-v2.md) e preserve autorização, Git e proteção de banco.
-
-## Criar, reutilizar e retomar
-
-1. Confirme raiz Git, diretório comum, branch/base e ownership. Não derive identidade só do path; não aproprie worktree de outro lote.
-2. No lote V2, use `flow prepare` para criar em branch final, preparar contexto e registrar recibo. Fora dele, o criador autorizado chama automaticamente `scripts/preparar-contexto.mjs --project RAIZ_REAL_DA_WORKTREE` desta pasta. Resolva o path a partir da skill, não de um drive fixo.
-3. Exija exit 0, `prepared:true`, raiz correta e caminho do banco isolado antes de delegar. Runtime/permissão/topologia indisponível é bloqueio real; continue as tarefas independentes.
-4. `ensure` é idempotente, preserva configuração, registra defaults locais e reindexa. Não altera arquivos rastreados nem instala hooks por padrão. Pode receber `--config-from RAIZ_CONFIRMADA` para herdar somente configuração pertinente; não copia índices, eventos, gates, credenciais ou aprovações.
-
-O SQLite vive em `_shared/.contexto/` da instalação local escolhida por regra fixa. Sem skills copiadas na worktree, o helper cria somente `.agents/skills/_shared/.contexto/`. A CLI embarcada pode ser chamada da instalação central com `--project` apontando para a worktree; os dados ficam na raiz selecionada, não na fonte central. Cada executor usa sua raiz explícita. Configuração legada em `.contexto/` continua válida; não migre/copiem estados silenciosamente.
-
-`setup` existe para compatibilidade e registro explícito; o fluxo usa ensure automaticamente. Hooks antigos permanecem preservados; nenhum hook novo é necessário nesta distribuição. Não configure um MCP global para aprovar outra raiz.
-
-## Limpeza
-
-Encerre executores e use `flow cleanup-check` antes de `flow cleanup` no lote. Fora dele, `archive --project RAIZ_REAL` apenas preserva o histórico e informa `archived:true`/`cleanup_safe`; não remove a worktree nem prova ausência de executores.
-
-Ownership, topologia, branch preservada, estado Git limpo, ausência de operação pendente e de ignorados únicos continuam obrigatórios. Links/junctions, node_modules, arquivos operacionais desconhecidos ou atividade concorrente bloqueiam remoção. Nunca exclusão recursiva/force, nunca limpeza de worktree externa ao lote. Arquivo histórico não reativa gates em outra raiz.

----
-name: archify
-description: "Create validated architecture, workflow, sequence, data-flow, lifecycle/state, ERD, class, tree, timeline, and waterfall diagrams as explorable standalone HTML with dark/light themes, motion and image/SVG/WebM export. Accept requirements or Mermaid; inspect repository evidence for code-backed diagrams. Use when visualizing systems, API calls, pipelines, schemas, histories, timings, or everyday steps, parts, relationships and states. Also turn an answer into a one-page explainer, with the conclusion first, structured panels, native diagrams and charts, when the user asks for a page, an explainer or an answer to share (做成一页, 用页面讲), or proactively when the user's rules opt in with an [archify explainer: ...] line. Not for dashboards."
-license: Apache-2.0
-metadata:
-  version: "3.2"
-  author: tt-a1i
----
-
-# Archify
-
-Create checked standalone HTML as a native diagram or a one-page explainer that answers a question.
-
-Run commands from your working directory. Unless the user names another location, give each new artifact request its own folder `.archify/<type>-<slug>-<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS>/` there (local time, chosen once): keep the candidate and `<slug>.html` in it and reuse it for repairs. Native diagrams use `candidate.json` with `meta.output` relative to the working directory; explainers may use `candidate.archify.md` and a portable output filename. A later request gets a new folder. Replace `bin/archify.mjs` in every command with the installed package's absolute path, or its path relative to your working directory; CLI input and output paths resolve from that directory.
-
-For a native diagram of a real codebase, read [Repository authoring](references/repository-authoring.md) while tracing the requested behavior. A system description uses the native steps below; a frozen candidate uses the handoff path.
-
-## Choose the artifact
-
-- When the user asks to draw or visualize a system, flow, schema or history, use a native diagram and the Type router.
-- Use `explainer` when the user asks for the answer as a page: a page, one page, an explainer, something to share (“做成一页”, “用页面讲”, “answer with a page”). Without such a request, answer in text or draw the requested diagram. A page made on request ends its reply with the one-line mode offer under Output.
-- A rules line in context changes this. `[archify explainer: proactive]`: also make a page, unasked, for an explanation, comparison, trade-off, decision, diagnosis, review or plan that needs a table, steps or several sections. `[archify explainer: always-on]`: every reply that reaches a conclusion also gets a compact page of at most four panels, delivered without opening it, its link closing the reply. `[archify explainer: on-demand]`: only when asked, and never offer a mode.
-- In every mode a page needs a conclusion with some structure behind it: chat, one-line answers, raw command output and text-only requests get none.
-- For `explainer`, read [Explainer authoring](references/explainer-authoring.md) for its conclusion, reasons, scope, board layout and optional native diagrams. Write the complete draft, then run `finalize explainer` for validation, atomic delivery and artifact checks. Use panel patch for local content revisions.
-
-## Existing candidate handoff
-
-When the user supplies a frozen candidate, run `finalize` first as one CLI invocation. Its passing receipt completes the automated gates; follow any visual review recommendation under Delivery before claiming visual quality. For repair, follow step 5.
-
-`finalize` includes a bounded update check in its delivery receipt; see Update awareness.
-
-## Native diagram authoring
-
-Use this path for ordinary generation. Read branch references only when their stated trigger applies.
-
-1. Choose `architecture`, `workflow`, `sequence`, `dataflow`, `lifecycle`, `erd`, `class`, `tree`, `timeline`, or `waterfall` from the question.
-2. Use the exact schema and example paths in the Type router without listing their directories. Read [Authoring defaults](references/authoring-defaults.md) and the mode's example in a bounded batch separate from project documents and complete schemas so neither is truncated; recover any missing section before writing. For Architecture, use the matching showcase example. For every mode except Architecture, also read the mode and common schemas. Read the relevant schema definition before choosing any new field, enum, or constrained text, especially boundary kinds. Examples teach shape, not facts. Use fresh IDs, wording, and layout. Go directly to the candidate without preliminary help, doctor, starter validation, temporary diagrams, or output-path listing. Query brands only for an explicitly requested mark; read [Brand marks](references/brand-marks.md) for an unknown mark with a user-provided URL.
-3. Once the requested scope and, for a real codebase, [source evidence](references/repository-authoring.md) are covered, write the complete candidate directly without planning coordinates in prose. Choose Architecture abstraction and connected placement using Authoring defaults before coordinates: show the main user journey and necessary branches, preserve control roles and behavior-changing conditions, and leave enough room for actual relationship labels. No node, relationship, source, view, card, or boundary count is a target or ceiling. Use automatic routes first; add explicit routing only for necessary branch, return, supplied geometry, or measured repair. Set `meta.quality_profile` to `"showcase"` unless the user requests dense `standard`. For ERD, use a table-first layout: show every physical column in `entities[].attributes`, keep its SQL type and source comment, state every key role a column carries (`key` takes a role or a list, so a junction column is `["pk", "fk"]`, and every `fk` column also needs `references` like `"orders.id"`), and never move columns into cards as a substitute for the table. Classify tables into functional domains before placement, give each domain a concise `tag`, and place its members in one solid rectangle of grid cells — a single row, a single column, or a filled rectangular block, not an L or diagonal. A tagged table always needs `row`/`col`, because absolute coordinates have no grid cells and a domain whose tables do not fill one rectangle cannot be drawn as a band: the renderer reports `erd/domain-not-drawn` instead of publishing a diagram that cannot name the domain. A multi-domain schema reads best as one domain per column — each `tag` a vertical run — because the reader scales a wide canvas up to the reader width and shrinks a tall one until the page fits, so the wide arrangement is the one that stays complete and legible inside a laptop viewport. A schema-first ERD over roughly 8 tables or 50 fields is itself a dense map: author its first complete-field pass at `standard` and upgrade only once the layout still reads.
-4. Once the complete first candidate is written, run `finalize` directly. Its first gate is showcase validation; successful first drafts need no separate pre-validation. Keep the candidate unchanged while the command runs:
-
-   ```bash
-   node bin/archify.mjs finalize <type> <candidate.json> <output.html> --quality showcase --json
-   ```
-
-   For a repository-backed candidate, include evidence on the first draft and use the complete first command: `node bin/archify.mjs finalize <type> <candidate.json> <output.html> --repo-root <repo-root> --quality showcase --json`. Pass the `--quality` that matches `meta.quality_profile`, such as `standard` for a dense first ERD pass.
-
-   A passing receipt proves the included `validate`, `deliver`, strict `check`, and real-browser `browser-check` gates passed. Use its compact summary; run standalone commands only for a separate request or focused failure diagnosis.
-
-5. A non-zero exit is never success. Read compact stdout or `evidence.summaryReceipt`, then [repair the failed gate](references/delivery-contract.md#failed-finalize-and-candidate-repair), including its repair limit. Preserve requested meaning and source evidence. For several tangled Architecture routes, read [Architecture layout repair](references/architecture-layout-repair.md); for measured field or geometry failures, read [Authoring contract](references/authoring-contract.md). Edit the connected neighborhood and rerun the complete `finalize` command from step 4. Once a run has reached `browser-check`, the output path owns that evidence: give every later run its own `--out-dir <folder>/review-<n>`.
-
-## Update awareness
-
-`finalize` and standalone `deliver` include `update` in their receipts. Do not run a separate check for the same delivery. If `update.noticeRequired` is true, read `references/update-awareness.md` and keep one compact update notice in your final response to the user, even after a quality gate fails. For a task with several diagrams, mention the update once in the final response. Snooze or ignore a reminder only when the user explicitly asks; never install or update on your own initiative.
-
-Before the first candidate, use the authoring references and relevant repository source, not Archify implementation or tests. Inspect Archify implementation if diagnostics remain unactionable after focused repairs.
-
-
-## Type router
-
-| Type | Use for | Schema | Example |
-|---|---|---|---|
-| `architecture` | Components, services, cloud/security boundaries, infrastructure; what something everyday is made of | `schemas/architecture.schema.json` | System descriptions, services, libraries, and CLI repos: `examples/web-app.architecture.json`; deployment repos: `examples/production-deployment.architecture.json` |
-| `workflow` | Processes, approval gates, tool calls, runbooks, CI/CD; plans and step-by-step life processes | `schemas/workflow.schema.json` | `examples/agent-tool-call.workflow.json` |
-| `sequence` | API call chains, request lifecycles, async traces, returns; back-and-forth between people | `schemas/sequence.schema.json` | `examples/cache-miss-request.sequence.json` |
-| `dataflow` | Pipelines, ETL/ELT, lineage, governance, consumers; where money or documents go | `schemas/dataflow.schema.json` | `examples/product-analytics.dataflow.json` |
-| `lifecycle` | State/status transitions, retries, waiting and terminal states; where an application or order stands | `schemas/lifecycle.schema.json` | `examples/deployment-release.lifecycle.json` |
-| `erd` | Tables/entities, attributes, primary/foreign/unique keys, cardinality between them | `schemas/erd.schema.json` | `examples/orders.erd.json` |
-| `tree` | Single-parent containment: repository/module trees, capability or feature breakdowns, org-style decomposition | `schemas/tree.schema.json` | `examples/payment-platform.tree.json` |
-| `class` | Classes, interfaces, selected members, and dependency/association/inheritance/realization/composition between types | `schemas/class.schema.json` | `examples/payments.class.json` |
-| `timeline` | When things happened: incident reviews, release histories, timestamped events on a proportional clock with source lanes | `schemas/timeline.schema.json` | `examples/payment-incident.timeline.json` |
-| `waterfall` | Where the time went: span durations, overlap, and nesting of one request or agent run on a common time axis | `schemas/waterfall.schema.json` | `examples/checkout-request.waterfall.json` |
-
-When choosing among native diagram types is ambiguous, run `node bin/archify.mjs guide "<scenario>" --json`. Scenario proof examples are structural references, not facts to copy.
-
-For an everyday subject, keep the same diagram modes and semantic types, then name them for the reader: use everyday `icon` values and `meta.legend` labels as in [Node icons](references/authoring-contract.md#node-icons). Ask for missing personal facts instead of inventing dates, amounts, or rules.
-
-## Mermaid input
-
-Read Mermaid for topology and meaning, then author fresh Archify JSON; do not mechanically render Mermaid styling.
-
-- `flowchart` / `graph` → `workflow`, or `architecture` for a component map.
-- `sequenceDiagram` → `sequence`; participants become semantic participants and arrows become messages.
-- `stateDiagram` → `lifecycle`; states and transitions retain meaning, not Mermaid style.
-- `erDiagram` → `erd`; entity and relationship names, keys, and cardinality retain meaning, not Mermaid style.
-- `classDiagram` → `class`; type kinds, selected members, and relationship kinds retain meaning, not Mermaid style.
-
-## Delivery
-
-Use the `finalize` command above for the first candidate and after a repair.
-
-`finalize` stops at the first non-passing gate. Its compact stdout and `<output-stem>.finalize-summary.json` are ordinary evidence. A passing run creates no screenshots and reports `visualReview: "not-requested"`.
-
-When a passing Architecture receipt reports `visualReviewRecommendation.signals.resolvedCrossovers`, copy the candidate aside and apply the hints in one edit that changes only node positions and sizes: every node, relationship (including its `from` and `to`), label, and source stays as it was. Rerun the complete `finalize` once with `--out-dir <folder>/review-2`, because the previous HTML already owns its browser evidence. `--out-dir` relocates the new browser-check and default finalize receipts, not the HTML or its delivery receipt. Successful delivery rewrites that pair at the requested output path; earlier review evidence remains bound to its original artifact bytes. See [review evidence paths](references/delivery-contract.md#a-new-candidate-at-an-existing-output-path). If that run fails, reports more crossings, or reports the same crossings with more `signals.routesOverSuggestedBends`, restore the copy and finalize it with `--out-dir <folder>/review-3`. Do not start a second placement round. Hints about extra bends alone are optional.
-
-When `layoutReviewRecommendation.action` is `inspect-sequence-width`, follow [Sequence width review](references/delivery-contract.md#sequence-width-review) before handing off a newly authored Sequence.
-
-Perceptual review is optional for ordinary generation, including a newly positioned Architecture. Use [Optional capture evidence](references/delivery-contract.md#optional-capture-evidence), with `--out-dir <folder>/visual-check`, when the user requests visual review, during development audits, or for a concrete route/browser concern. `visualReviewRecommendation` is advisory. Inspect captures before claiming visual quality; qualify any check claim as automated when perceptual review has not occurred.
-
-Read [Delivery contract](references/delivery-contract.md) for failed gates, standalone commands, provenance/recovery, repeated delivery, exports, or opening. Native diagram recovery follows `deliver` → strict provenance `check` → `browser-check`; captures require strict provenance. Explainer delivery uses validate, deliver and check as described in its authoring guide.
-
-For workflow viewport overflow, read [Workflow viewport repair](references/authoring-contract.md#workflow-viewport-repair) before the next layout edit.
-
-When reporting verification details, distinguish artifact checks, browser evidence, captures, and actual perceptual review. For an explicitly requested immediate preview or active desktop loop, see [Optional opening](references/delivery-contract.md#optional-opening).
-
-## Optional viewer capabilities
-
-Live motion is enabled by default for every rendered diagram; omit `meta.animation`. The Viewer’s Live/Still button controls playback.
-
-Read `references/viewer-runtime.md` only when the user explicitly asks for Share Cards, Route/Reach cards, motion, deep links, presentation, search/focus, or another Viewer Runtime feature.
-
-## Setup and fallback
-
-No install is required inside the skill package. For setup diagnosis, verify with:
-
-```bash
-node bin/archify.mjs doctor
-node bin/archify.mjs demo <output-directory>
-```
-
-For native diagrams, when shell access is unavailable, hand-place architecture SVG into `assets/template.html`, use CSS semantic classes rather than inline colors, and follow the visual review contract in `references/delivery-contract.md`. Explainers require their renderer and real delivery gates; if those are unavailable, report the limitation and give a text answer when useful, without claiming HTML delivery.
-
-## Output
-
-Reply in the user's language, as briefly as the result allows; the diagram carries the content, so a single diagram usually needs one line.
-
-- Lead with a clickable Markdown link to the HTML: a descriptive title, not the file name, and its absolute path, wrapped in `<...>` when it contains spaces.
-- When the user wants to understand a system or codebase rather than draw a described subject, add one or two sentences with the key takeaway. Skip sentences that only restate what the diagram obviously shows.
-- State anything that changes how the diagram should be read: the abstraction level or deliberately omitted parts when a reader might expect them, illustrative rather than measured values, missing source evidence, or requested content dropped or merged during repair.
-- For several diagrams, report completion once with a link to an existing overview or compact per-diagram links, not a directory path.
-
-Do not recap commands, repair rounds, hashes, quality profiles, or check lists; they stay in the receipts. If asked whether the diagram was verified, answer in one line, such as “Automated checks passed; not visually reviewed.” Give receipt links and details only for reproducibility or troubleshooting. Disclose requested visual review that could not run, and claim visual inspection only when performed. Keep the required update notice under Update awareness.
-
-Example: `Created [Checkout request timing](/abs/path/checkout-timing.html). Durations are illustrative, not measured.`
-
-For an explainer, reply in two or three lines: the conclusion and the page link. Mention gates only when one failed or writing warnings remain; do not paste the draft.
-
-After an explainer made on request, when no `[archify explainer: ...]` line is in context, end the reply with one optional line offering the proactive mode, once per conversation, for example: “需要的话，以后遇到解释、对比、排查这类问题，我可以主动做成这样的页面，要开启吗？” If the user accepts, add `[archify explainer: proactive] Make an Archify explainer page, unasked, for explanations, comparisons, decisions, diagnoses, reviews and plans that need a table, steps or several sections.` to the global rules file of the current agent (such as `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`, `~/.codex/AGENTS.md` or `~/.config/devin/AGENTS.md`) and name the file; deleting the line turns it off. If the user declines, offer to add `[archify explainer: on-demand]` so the question does not return.
diff --git a/.agents/skills/archify/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md b/.agents/skills/archify/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md

@@ -1,78 +0,0 @@
-# Third-party notices
-
-Archify includes optional vector data for third-party brand marks. These marks
-are provided only to identify technologies and services in user-authored
-diagrams. Their inclusion does not imply sponsorship, endorsement, partnership,
-or affiliation with Archify.
-
-Archify's license and historical MIT grants are described in LICENSE, NOTICE,
-and LICENSE-MIT. The software license does not
-replace the copyright licenses, trademark policies, or brand guidelines that
-apply to third-party marks. Users are responsible for confirming that their
-particular use is permitted.
-
-## Simple Icons
-
-Most of the built-in vector paths and their metadata were generated from
-[Simple Icons 16.28.0](https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons/tree/16.28.0).
-Simple Icons makes its collection work available under
-[CC0 1.0 Universal](https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons/blob/16.28.0/LICENSE.md).
-
-As Simple Icons explains in its
-[disclaimer](https://github.com/simple-icons/simple-icons/blob/16.28.0/DISCLAIMER.md),
-CC0 for the collection does not mean that every underlying icon is CC0. License
-and brand-guideline metadata may be incomplete or change over time. The absence
-of an individual license entry is not a grant of permission.
-
-Archify embeds the selected icons as vector-path data and may render them in a
-user-selected color. The following individual licenses were recorded in the
-pinned Simple Icons 16.28.0 metadata:
-
-| Mark | Recorded source | Recorded license | Archify treatment |
-|---|---|---|---|
-| Angular | [Angular press kit](https://angular.dev/press-kit) | [`CC-BY-4.0`](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) | Embedded as vector-path data; color may be changed by the authored diagram. |
-| Apache Airflow | [Apache logos](https://apache.org/logos) | [`Apache-2.0`](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) | Embedded as vector-path data; Apache trademarks remain subject to the [ASF trademark policy](https://www.apache.org/foundation/marks/). |
-| Apache Kafka | [Apache logos](https://apache.org/logos) | [`Apache-2.0`](https://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0) | Embedded as vector-path data; Apache trademarks remain subject to the [ASF trademark policy](https://www.apache.org/foundation/marks/). |
-| .NET | [.NET brand repository](https://github.com/dotnet/brand/blob/c7d0f51b8ec59531332d05fb27a5b758a7a3d689/logo/dotnet-logo.svg) | [`CC0-1.0`](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/) | Embedded as vector-path data; color may be changed by the authored diagram. |
-| JavaScript | [JS community logo](https://github.com/voodootikigod/logo.js/blob/1544bdeed6d618a6cfe4f0650d04ab8d9cfa76d9/js.svg) | [`MIT`](https://github.com/voodootikigod/logo.js/blob/1544bdeed6d618a6cfe4f0650d04ab8d9cfa76d9/LICENSE) | Embedded as vector-path data; color may be changed by the authored diagram. |
-| Jenkins | [Jenkins artwork source](https://get.jenkins.io/art/) | [`CC-BY-SA-3.0`](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/) | Embedded as vector-path data; color may be changed by the authored diagram. Jenkins retains its trademark rights. |
-| Rust | [Rust project](https://www.rust-lang.org) | [`CC-BY-SA-4.0`](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/) | Embedded as vector-path data; color may be changed by the authored diagram. See the [Rust media guide](https://www.rust-lang.org/policies/media-guide). |
-| Vue.js | [Vue logo source](https://github.com/vuejs/art/blob/a1c78b74569b70a25300925b4eacfefcc143b8f6/logo.svg) | [`CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0`](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/) | Embedded as vector-path data; color may be changed by the authored diagram. The non-commercial and share-alike conditions remain applicable; see the [Vue artwork terms](https://github.com/vuejs/art/blob/a1c78b74569b70a25300925b4eacfefcc143b8f6/README.md). |
-
-The source, guideline, and known license fields for every packaged mark are
-preserved in `renderers/shared/generated-brand-marks.mjs`.
-
-## OpenAI mark
-
-The OpenAI vector path is recorded from the
-[OpenAI brand guidelines](https://openai.com/brand/), not from Simple Icons.
-Use remains subject to those current guidelines and any applicable trademark
-rights. Its inclusion does not state or imply endorsement by OpenAI.
-
-## JetBrains Mono
-
-Delivered Archify viewer artifacts embed the JetBrains Mono variable font
-subsets served by Google Fonts. For characters covered by these subsets, font
-selection does not depend on a network request or a locally installed copy.
-Uncovered characters (including CJK) still use the system fallback stack;
-browser and operating-system rasterization can differ.
-JetBrains Mono is maintained at
-[github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono](https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono)
-and is distributed under the SIL Open Font License 1.1. The complete license
-text is preserved in `assets/JetBrainsMono-OFL.txt` in the packaged Skill and
-in the font CSS carried by standalone HTML and SVG exports.
-
-## Pele
-
-The explainer renders Mermaid chart fences with an unmodified subset of
-[Pele 1.3.0](https://github.com/obsidianmd/pele), copyright (c) 2026 kepano,
-distributed under the MIT License. The subset and its license text are in
-`explainer/vendor/pele/` in the packaged Skill. Charts are rendered to static
-SVG when a page is built; delivered pages contain no Pele code.
-
-## No additional rights granted
-
-Brand names, logos, and trademarks remain the property of their respective
-owners. This notice records provenance and known terms; it does not grant rights
-that Archify does not hold, and it does not state that every packaged mark has
-been cleared for every commercial, promotional, or redistributive use.

-    // Resolve the theme before first paint so light-preference users don't
-    // see a dark flash. The toolbar script below re-applies with UI state.
-    (function () {
-      try {
-        var theme = null;
-        try {
-          var param = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('theme');
-          if (param === 'light' || param === 'dark') theme = param;
-          if (new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('embed') === '1') {
-            document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-embed', 'true');
-          }
-          if (new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('present') === '1') {
-            document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-present', 'true');
-          }
-        } catch (_) {}
-        if (!theme) {
-          try { theme = localStorage.getItem('archify-theme'); } catch (_) {}
-        }
-        if (theme !== 'light' && theme !== 'dark') {
-          theme = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches ? 'light' : 'dark';
-        }
-        document.documentElement.setAttribute('data-theme', theme);
-      } catch (_) {}
-    })();

-    /* The reader owns only the outer scale. Compact automatic sequences fit at

-    /* Diagram Guide keeps the artifact's growing reader vocabulary

-       production interaction instead of creating a second command system. */

-      position: absolute;
-      top: 1rem;
-      right: 1rem;

-    .node-outline-item:hover::after,

-    .node-outline-item[aria-current="true"] { background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--outline-tone) 10%, transparent); }
-    .node-outline-item[aria-current="true"]::after { opacity: 0; }
-    /* Swatches echo the diagram's node cards: tinted fill, hairline stroke. */
-    .node-outline-dot {
-      width: 0.625rem;
-      height: 0.5rem;
-      border: 1.25px solid var(--outline-tone);
-      border-radius: 0.15rem;
-      background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--outline-tone) 16%, var(--bg));

-    .node-outline-item:hover .node-outline-dot,

-      overflow: hidden;
-      font-size: 0.8125rem;
-      font-weight: 500;
-      text-overflow: ellipsis;

-    }
-    .node-outline-item[aria-current="true"] strong { font-weight: 600; }

-      overflow: hidden;

-      white-space: nowrap;

-    .node-outline-item:hover small,
-    .node-outline-item[data-previewing] small,

-
-    /* The desktop bottom rail is an index: compact rows keep related nodes
-       together while allowing full names and descriptions to wrap naturally. */
-    html[data-reader-rail="bottom"] .node-outline-item {
-      grid-template-columns: 0.625rem minmax(0, 1fr) 0.75rem;

-      padding-block: 0.375rem;

-    .card-header {
-      display: flex;
-      align-items: center;
-      gap: 0.5rem;
-      margin-bottom: 0.625rem;
-    }
-
-    .card-dot {
-      flex: none;
-      width: 8px;
-      height: 8px;
-      border-radius: 50%;
-    }
-
-    .card-dot.cyan     { background: var(--frontend-stroke); }
-    .card-dot.emerald  { background: var(--backend-stroke); }
-    .card-dot.violet   { background: var(--database-stroke); }
-    .card-dot.amber    { background: var(--cloud-stroke); }
-    .card-dot.rose     { background: var(--security-stroke); }
-    .card-dot.orange   { background: var(--messagebus-stroke); }
-    .card-dot.slate    { background: var(--external-stroke); }
-
-    .card h3 { font-size: 0.9375rem; font-weight: 600; line-height: 1.4; color: var(--text); }
-
-    .card ul {
-      list-style: none;
-      color: var(--text-muted);
-      font-size: 0.8125rem;
-      line-height: 1.6;
-    }
-
-    .card li {
-      position: relative;
-      margin-bottom: 0.3rem;
-      padding-left: 0.9rem;
-    }
-    .card li:last-child { margin-bottom: 0; }
-    /* Hanging markers take the card's tone so wrapped lines align under text. */
-    .card li::before {
-      position: absolute;
-      top: calc(0.8em - 2px);
-      left: 0.2rem;
-      width: 4px;
-      height: 4px;
-      border-radius: 50%;
-      background: color-mix(in srgb, var(--card-tone, var(--text-muted)) 70%, transparent);
-      content: "";
-    }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.cyan)    { --card-tone: var(--frontend-stroke); }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.emerald) { --card-tone: var(--backend-stroke); }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.violet)  { --card-tone: var(--database-stroke); }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.amber)   { --card-tone: var(--cloud-stroke); }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.rose)    { --card-tone: var(--security-stroke); }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.orange)  { --card-tone: var(--messagebus-stroke); }
-    .card:has(.card-dot.slate)   { --card-tone: var(--external-stroke); }
-    .card-dot { box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px color-mix(in srgb, var(--card-tone, transparent) 16%, transparent); }

-    /* ==========================================================
-       Print stylesheet — hide interactive controls, force light,
-       drop the grid so the diagram doesn't waste ink, use landscape
-       so wide diagrams fit, pack summary cards into 2 columns to
-       avoid an orphan card on a trailing page.
-       ========================================================== */
-    @page { size: landscape; margin: 1.5cm; }
-
-    @media print {
-      /* Force the FULL light palette — including component fills/strokes and
-         lane/arrow colors — so printing from dark theme doesn't put neon
-         strokes and translucent dark fills on white paper. */
-      :root, [data-theme="dark"], [data-theme="light"] {
-        --bg: #ffffff;
-        --grid: transparent;
-        --panel: #ffffff;
-        --panel-border: #e2e8f0;
-        --text: #0f172a;
-        --text-muted: #475569;
-        --text-dim: #94a3b8;
-        --text-faint: #64748b;
-        --mask: #ffffff;
-        --lane-fill: rgba(248, 250, 252, 0.65);
-        --lane-stroke: #cbd5e1;
-        --arrow: #94a3b8;
-        --arrow-emphasis: #059669;
-        --frontend-fill:    rgba(34, 211, 238, 0.15);
-        --frontend-stroke:  #0891b2;
-        --backend-fill:     rgba(52, 211, 153, 0.18);
-        --backend-stroke:   #059669;
-        --database-fill:    rgba(167, 139, 250, 0.2);
-        --database-stroke:  #7c3aed;
-        --cloud-fill:       rgba(251, 191, 36, 0.18);
-        --cloud-stroke:     #d97706;
-        --security-fill:    rgba(251, 113, 133, 0.15);
-        --security-stroke:  #e11d48;
-        --messagebus-fill:  rgba(251, 146, 60, 0.15);
-        --messagebus-stroke:#ea580c;
-        --external-fill:    rgba(148, 163, 184, 0.18);
-        --external-stroke:  #64748b;
-      }
-      body { background: #ffffff !important; padding: 0; }
-      .container { max-width: none; }
-      .toolbar, .diagram-nav, .focus-chip, .archify-toast, .no-print { display: none !important; }
-      
-      .diagram-container, .card { box-shadow: none; border-color: #e2e8f0; }
-      .diagram-container { --archify-nav-reserve: 0px !important; }
-      html[data-preset="signal-flow"] .diagram-container,
-      html[data-preset="signal-flow"] .card { background: #ffffff; }
-      .cards { grid-template-columns: 1fr 1fr; }
-      /* Ensure elements break sensibly across pages */
-      .card { break-inside: avoid; page-break-inside: avoid; }
-      .diagram-container { break-inside: avoid; page-break-inside: avoid; }
-      .diagram-container svg [data-detail] {
-        opacity: 1 !important;
-        pointer-events: auto !important;
-      }
-      .diagram-container svg [data-detail-anchor] { transform: none !important; }
-      .diagram-container svg[data-lens-active] [data-node-id],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-lens-active] [data-edge-from],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-legend-preview-active] [data-node-id],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-legend-preview-active] [data-edge-from] {
-        opacity: 1 !important;
-        filter: none !important;
-      }
-      [data-legend-bridge-runtime] { display: none !important; }
-      .semantic-lens-overlay { display: none !important; }
-      .relationship-hit-overlay { display: none !important; }
-      .relationship-pulse-overlay { display: none !important; }
-      .route-probe-overlay, .route-journey-overlay { display: none !important; }
-      .diagram-container svg[data-focus-active] [data-node-id],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-focus-active] [data-edge-from],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-focus-active] [data-graph-role="automatic-crossover-underlay"],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-reach-active] [data-node-id],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-reach-active] [data-edge-from],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-reach-active] [data-graph-role="automatic-crossover-underlay"],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-route-active] [data-node-id],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-route-active] [data-edge-from],
-      .diagram-container svg[data-route-active] [data-graph-role="automatic-crossover-underlay"] {
-        opacity: 1 !important;
-        filter: none !important;
-        animation: none !important;
-      }
-      h1, .subtitle { color: #0f172a; }
-    }

-    /* ==========================================================
-       TOOLBAR (theme toggle + export menu)
-       ========================================================== */
-    /* The toolbar tracks the centered reader column and the title row, so
-       an adaptive narrow reader does not leave its controls stranded at the
-       viewport edge. */
-    .toolbar {
-      position: absolute;
-      top: var(--archify-page-top);
-      right: max(1rem, calc((100vw - min(100vw - 4rem, var(--archify-reader-width, 1440px))) / 2));
-      display: flex;
-      align-items: center;
-      gap: 0.125rem;
-      padding: 0;
-      border: 0;
-      background: transparent;
-      box-shadow: none;
-      z-index: 100;
-    }
-    /* Ghost controls keep a 44px hit area while the visible pill stays compact;
-       Export is the one primary action. */
-    .toolbar button {
-      position: relative;
-      isolation: isolate;
-      background: transparent;
-      color: var(--text-muted);
-      border: 0;
-      padding: 0.5rem 0.75rem;
-      border-radius: 0.5625rem;
-      font-family: inherit;
-      font-size: 0.8125rem;
-      font-weight: 500;
-      cursor: pointer;
-      white-space: nowrap;
-      box-shadow: none;
-      transition: color 0.15s;
-      display: inline-flex;
-      align-items: center;
-      gap: 0.4rem;
-      min-height: 2.75rem;
-    }
-    .toolbar button::before {
-      position: absolute;
-      z-index: -1;
-      inset: 0.375rem 0;

-      background: transparent;

-    /* Reading Depth is a viewer-only level-of-detail layer. MAP preserves the

-    /* Live plays one relay per cycle: a comet (halo, tail, head) leaves each
-       source when the signal reaches it, travels at one shared speed, leaves a
-       soft wake, and lands as a ripple while its target glows. Downstream edges
-       depart only after their source is reached, so the reader sees the path the
-       diagram describes rather than every edge shimmering at once. Sequence
-       messages relay in authored chronological order. Motion Governor plans the
-       timeline and its per-edge keyframes; this stylesheet owns appearance.
-       Original line language and markers remain static. Node entry is bounded to
-       one pass per document. */
-    svg[data-animation="trace"] {
-      --flow-cycle: 6.4s;
-      --flow-halo-peak: 0.17;
-      --flow-glow-peak: 0.5;
-      --flow-tail-peak: 0.42;
-      --flow-head-peak: 0.95;
-      --flow-wake-peak: 0.3;

-    }

-      pointer-events: none;

-  <div class="container">
-    <!-- Header -->

-      <div class="header-row"
-           data-preset-badge-signal-flow="{{i18n:viewer.preset.badge.signalFlow}}"

-    <!-- ARCHIFY:SOURCE_EVIDENCE_DATA -->

-    <!-- Main Diagram -->
-    <div class="diagram-container" data-detail-level="read"
-         data-preset-badge-editorial-plate="{{i18n:viewer.preset.badge.editorialPlate}}">
-      <!-- ARCHIFY:SVG_SLOT_START -->
-      <svg viewBox="0 0 1000 680" role="img" aria-label="[PROJECT NAME] architecture diagram">
-        <!-- Definitions -->
-        <defs>
-          <marker id="arrowhead" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
-            <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" class="m-default" />
-          </marker>
-          <marker id="arrowhead-emphasis" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">
-            <polygon points="0 0, 10 3.5, 0 7" class="m-emphasis" />
-          </marker>
-          <marker id="arrowhead-security" markerWidth="10" markerHeight="7" refX="9" refY="3.5" orient="auto">

-  <script>
-    var Archify = {};
-    var archifyI18nData = (function () {
-      var node = document.getElementById('archify-i18n-data');
-      try { return JSON.parse(node ? node.textContent : '{}'); }
-      catch (_) { return { locale: 'en', messages: {} }; }
-    })();
-    Archify.locale = archifyI18nData.locale || 'en';
-
-    function viewerText(key, values) {
-      var messages = archifyI18nData.messages || {};
-      var template = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(messages, key) ? messages[key] : key;
-      return String(template).replace(/\{([a-zA-Z0-9_]+)\}/g, function (match, name) {
-        return values && Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(values, name) ? String(values[name]) : match;
-      });
-    }
-
-    function viewerCount(key, count, values) {
-      var suffix = Number(count) === 1 ? '.one' : '.other';
-      var payload = Object.assign({}, values || {}, { count: count });
-      return viewerText(key + suffix, payload);
-    }
-
-    function viewerKindLabel(value) {
-      var normalized = String(value || 'node').toLowerCase();
-      var knownKey = 'viewer.kind.' + normalized;
-      var known = viewerText(knownKey);
-      if (known !== knownKey) return known;
-      return normalized
-        .replace(/messagebus/gi, 'message bus')
-        .replace(/[-_]+/g, ' ')
-        .replace(/\b\w/g, function (letter) { return letter.toUpperCase(); });
-    }
-
-    function readerLink(state) {
-      var template = document.documentElement.getAttribute('data-reading-link-template');
-      if (template === null) return location.href.replace(/#.*$/, '') + '#' + state;
-      if (!template || template.length > 4096 || template.split('{state}').length !== 2) return null;
-      try {
-        var url = new URL(template.replace('{state}', encodeURIComponent(state)));
-        if (['http:', 'https:', 'file:'].indexOf(url.protocol) === -1 || url.username || url.password) return null;
-        return url.href;
-      } catch (_) { return null; }
-    }
-
-    function copyReaderText(value) {
-      function fallbackCopy() {
-        var field = document.createElement('textarea');
-        field.value = value;
-        field.setAttribute('readonly', '');
-        field.style.position = 'fixed';
-        field.style.opacity = '0';
-        document.body.appendChild(field);
-        field.select();
-        var copied = false;
-        try { copied = document.execCommand('copy'); } catch (_) {}
-        field.remove();
-        return copied;
-      }
-      var policy = document.permissionsPolicy || document.featurePolicy;
-      var allowed = !policy || typeof policy.allowsFeature !== 'function' || policy.allowsFeature('clipboard-write');
-      if (allowed && navigator.clipboard && typeof navigator.clipboard.writeText === 'function') {
-        try { return Promise.resolve(navigator.clipboard.writeText(value)).then(function () { return true; }).catch(fallbackCopy); }
-        catch (_) {}
-      }
-      return Promise.resolve(fallbackCopy());
-    }
-
-    function hasDrawableGeometry(element) {
-      if (!element || element.hasAttribute('data-ambient-flow-overlay')) return false;
-      var geometries = /^(path|line|polyline)$/i.test(element.tagName)
-        ? [element]
-        : Array.prototype.slice.call(element.querySelectorAll('path, line, polyline'));
-      return geometries.some(function (geometry) {
-        if (geometry.hasAttribute('data-ambient-flow-overlay')) return false;
-        var source = geometry.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'path'
-          ? geometry.getAttribute('d')
-          : geometry.tagName.toLowerCase() === 'polyline'
-            ? geometry.getAttribute('points')
-            : [geometry.getAttribute('x1'), geometry.getAttribute('y1'), geometry.getAttribute('x2'), geometry.getAttribute('y2')].join(' ');
-        if (!source || /(?:^|[^a-z])(?:nan|infinity)(?:[^a-z]|$)/i.test(source) || typeof geometry.getTotalLength !== 'function') return false;
-        try {
-          var length = Number(geometry.getTotalLength());
-          return Number.isFinite(length) && length > 0;
-        } catch (_) {
-          return false;
-        }
-      });
-    }
-
-    /* ============================================================
-       Visual style try-on — one topology, four bundled presets.
-       The reader's choice is intentionally session-only: it updates the
-       live page and canonical SVG together, but never rewrites the source,
-       URL, or a later diagram's authored default.
-       ============================================================ */
-    Archify.preset = (function () {
-      var PRESETS = ['classic', 'signal-flow', 'blueprint', 'editorial'];
-      var LABELS = {
-        classic: viewerText('viewer.preset.classic.short'),
-        'signal-flow': viewerText('viewer.preset.flow.short'),
-        blueprint: viewerText('viewer.preset.blueprint'),
-        editorial: viewerText('viewer.preset.editorial')
-      };
-      var html = document.documentElement;
-      var svg = document.querySelector('.diagram-container svg');
-      var btn = document.getElementById('btn-preset');
-      var label = document.getElementById('preset-label');
-      var menu = document.getElementById('preset-menu');
-      var options = function () {
-        return Array.prototype.slice.call(menu.querySelectorAll('[data-preset-value]'));
-      };
-      var authored = PRESETS.indexOf(html.getAttribute('data-preset')) >= 0
-        ? html.getAttribute('data-preset')
-        : 'classic';
-
-      function current() {
-        var value = html.getAttribute('data-preset');
-        return PRESETS.indexOf(value) >= 0 ? value : authored;
-      }
-      function nextAfter(preset) {
-        return PRESETS[(PRESETS.indexOf(preset) + 1) % PRESETS.length];
-      }
-      function apply(preset) {
-        if (html.getAttribute('data-embed') === 'true') return false;
-        if (PRESETS.indexOf(preset) < 0) return false;
-        html.setAttribute('data-preset', preset);
-        svg.setAttribute('data-preset', preset);
-        btn.setAttribute('data-preset-option', preset);
-        label.textContent = LABELS[preset];
-        btn.setAttribute('aria-label', viewerText('viewer.preset.current', { style: LABELS[preset] }));
-        btn.title = viewerText('viewer.preset.choose.title');
-        options().forEach(function (option) {
-          var selected = option.getAttribute('data-preset-value') === preset;
-          option.setAttribute('aria-checked', String(selected));
-        });
-        return true;
-      }
-      function cycle() { return apply(nextAfter(current())); }
-
-      function isOpen() { return menu.classList.contains('open'); }
-      function open(focusLast) {
-        if (html.getAttribute('data-embed') === 'true') return false;
-        if (Archify.exportMenu && Archify.exportMenu.isOpen()) Archify.exportMenu.close(false);
-        menu.classList.add('open');
-        btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'true');
-        var available = options();
-        var selected = available.find(function (option) { return option.getAttribute('aria-checked') === 'true'; });
-        var target = focusLast ? available[available.length - 1] : (selected || available[0]);
-        if (target) target.focus();
-        return true;
-      }
-      function close(focusTrigger) {
-        menu.classList.remove('open');
-        btn.setAttribute('aria-expanded', 'false');
-        if (focusTrigger) btn.focus();
-        return false;
-      }
-
-      apply(authored);
-      btn.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
-        e.stopPropagation();
-        if (isOpen()) close(false);
-        else open(false);
-      });
-      btn.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
-        if (e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || e.metaKey || e.shiftKey) return;
-        if (e.key === 'ArrowDown' || e.key === 'ArrowUp') {
-          e.preventDefault();
-          if (!isOpen()) open(e.key === 'ArrowUp');
-        }
-      });
-      document.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
-        if (!menu.contains(e.target) && e.target !== btn) close(false);
-      });
-      menu.addEventListener('click', function (e) {
-        var option = e.target.closest('[data-preset-value]');
-        if (!option || !menu.contains(option)) return;
-        if (apply(option.getAttribute('data-preset-value'))) close(true);
-      });
-      menu.addEventListener('keydown', function (e) {
-        if (e.key === 'Escape') { e.preventDefault(); close(true); return; }
-        if (e.key === 'Tab') { close(false); return; }
-        if (e.ctrlKey || e.altKey || e.metaKey || e.shiftKey) return;
-        var available = options();
-        var active = available.indexOf(document.activeElement);
-        switch (e.key) {
-          case 'ArrowDown':
-            e.preventDefault();
-            if (available.length) available[(active + 1 + available.length) % available.length].focus();
-            break;
-          case 'ArrowUp':
-            e.preventDefault();
-            if (available.length) available[(active - 1 + available.length) % available.length].focus();
-            break;
-          case 'Home':
-            e.preventDefault();
-            if (available[0]) available[0].focus();
-            break;
-          case 'End':
-            e.preventDefault();
-            if (available.length) available[available.length - 1].focus();
-            break;
-        }
-      });
-      return { cycle: cycle, apply: apply, current: current, authored: authored, open: open, close: close, isOpen: isOpen };
-    })();
-
-    /* ============================================================
-       Theme toggle — persists to localStorage, respects system pref
-       ============================================================ */
-
-    Archify.theme = (function () {
-      var STORAGE_KEY = 'archify-theme';
-      var html = document.documentElement;
-      var btn = document.getElementById('btn-theme');
-      var label = document.getElementById('theme-label');
-
-      // localStorage can throw (blocked cookies, sandboxed iframes); the whole
-      // script element dies on an uncaught error, so guard every access.
-      function readStored() {
-        try { return localStorage.getItem(STORAGE_KEY); } catch (_) { return null; }
-      }
-      function writeStored(value) {
-        try { localStorage.setItem(STORAGE_KEY, value); } catch (_) {}
-      }
-      function urlOverride() {
-        // URL param wins (useful for deterministic screenshots / share links)
-        try {
-          var param = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get('theme');
-          if (param === 'light' || param === 'dark') return param;
-        } catch (_) {}
-        return null;
-      }
-
-      function resolveInitial() {
-        var fromUrl = urlOverride();
-        if (fromUrl) return fromUrl;
-        var saved = readStored();
-        if (saved === 'light' || saved === 'dark') return saved;
-        return window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)').matches ? 'light' : 'dark';
-      }
-
-      function apply(theme) {
-        html.setAttribute('data-theme', theme);
-        label.textContent = viewerText(theme === 'dark' ? 'viewer.theme.dark' : 'viewer.theme.light');
-        btn.setAttribute('aria-pressed', theme === 'light' ? 'true' : 'false');
-      }
-
-      function toggle() {
-        var next = html.getAttribute('data-theme') === 'dark' ? 'light' : 'dark';
-        apply(next);
-        writeStored(next);
-      }
-
-      apply(resolveInitial());
-      btn.addEventListener('click', toggle);
-
-      // Follow live OS theme changes while the user has no explicit preference.
-      try {
-        var media = window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: light)');
-        var onChange = function (e) {
-          var saved = readStored();
-          if (urlOverride() || saved === 'light' || saved === 'dark') return;
-          apply(e.matches ? 'light' : 'dark');
-        };
-        if (media.addEventListener) media.addEventListener('change', onChange);
-        else if (media.addListener) media.addListener(onChange);
-      } catch (_) {}
-
-      return { toggle: toggle };
-    })();
-
-    /* ============================================================
-       Export — Share Card / PNG / JPEG / WebP / SVG / WebM and clipboard
-
-       Raster exports are always rendered at 4x source resolution for
-       maximum sharpness. The trick: we set the serialized SVG's
-       `width`/`height` to viewBox * 4 so the browser rasterizes the
-       vectors at that resolution natively. drawImage then draws at
-       the image's natural size (no upscaling = no blur).
-
-       JPEG/WebP paint the current theme's background explicitly since
-       those formats have no alpha channel.
-       ============================================================ */
-    (function () {
-      var RASTER_SCALE = 4;
-      var MOTION_DURATION = 6000;
-      var MOTION_FPS = 30;
-      var SHARE_CARD_WIDTH = 1200;
-      var SHARE_CARD_HEIGHT = 630;
-      var SHARE_CARD_PADDING = 40;
-      var SHARE_CARD_HEADER = 124;
-
-      function exportError(key, values) {
-        var error = new Error(viewerText(key, values));
-        error.archifyViewerMessage = true;
-        return error;
-      }
-
-      function exportMessage(error) {
-        return error && error.archifyViewerMessage
-          ? error.message
-          : viewerText('viewer.export.unknown');
-      }
-
-      function diagramFilename() {
-        var title = (document.title || 'diagram')
-          .replace(/\s+Architecture(\s+Diagram)?$/i, '')
-          .replace(/\s+Diagram$/i, '')
-          .trim();
-        return title.replace(/[^a-z0-9_\-]+/gi, '-')
-                    .toLowerCase()
-                    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '') || 'diagram';
-      }
-
-      function currentBg() {
-        return getComputedStyle(document.body).backgroundColor || '#ffffff';
-      }
-
-      function cleanExportClone(clone) {
-        Array.prototype.forEach.call(clone.querySelectorAll('[data-ambient-flow-overlay]'), function (el) {
-          el.remove();
-        });

-function pathEntryExists(file) {
-  try {
-    fs.lstatSync(file);

-  } catch (error) {
-    if (error.code === 'ENOENT' || error.code === 'ENOTDIR') return false;
-    throw error;

-function captureOwnedStagingFile(registry, filePath, fileBindingRuntime, {
-  subject = 'private-staging-entry',
-  content,
-  expectedLinks = 1,
-} = {}) {
-  const { captureRegularFileBinding } = fileBindingRuntime || {};
-  if (typeof captureRegularFileBinding !== 'function') {
-    throw new Error('The regular-file binding runtime is unavailable.');

-  let captured = captureRegularFileBinding(filePath, {
-    subject,
-    ...(content ? {
-      expectedSha256: content.sha256,
-      expectedBytes: content.bytes,

-    expectedLinks,

-        subject,

-        expectedLinks: observedLinks,

-function cleanupOwnedStagingDirectory(directory, identity, registry, fileBindingRuntime) {
-  const {
-    quarantineRemoveRegularFileBinding,
-    releaseRegularFileBinding,
-  } = fileBindingRuntime || {};
-  if (typeof quarantineRemoveRegularFileBinding !== 'function'
-    || typeof releaseRegularFileBinding !== 'function') {
-    throw new Error('The regular-file binding runtime is unavailable.');

-  for (const entry of [...registry].reverse()) {

-        subject: entry.subject,

-      // owned inode. Every other non-removal result is deliberately preserved:
-      // it may be a concurrent claimant rather than an entry we created.

-      failures.push(`${entry.filePath}: ${error.message}`);
-    } finally {

-      if (released.status !== 'released') {

-    if (!removeOwnedEmptyStagingDirectory(directory, identity, { throwOnFailure: true })) {

-  } catch (error) {

-function createOwnedEmptyStagingDirectory(prefix) {

-  // UNC prefix past MAX_PATH. Use the equivalent namespaced spelling for the
-  // syscall while preserving the same physical directory identity.

-  if (!metadata.isDirectory() || metadata.isSymbolicLink() || metadata.ino === 0n) {
-    throw new Error(`Private staging directory identity is unavailable: ${directory}`);
-  }
-  return {
-    directory,
-    identity: { device: metadata.dev, inode: metadata.ino },
-  };

-function createStagingRetirementQuarantine(parent) {
-  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 8; attempt += 1) {
-    const directory = path.join(parent, `.archify-staging-remove-${randomUUID()}`);

-      fs.mkdirSync(directory, { mode: 0o700 });
-      return directory;
-    } catch (error) {
-      if (error?.code !== 'EEXIST') return undefined;
-    }
-  }
-  return undefined;
-}

-const stagingRemovalSignal = new Int32Array(new SharedArrayBuffer(4));
-const stagingRemovalAttempts = 10;

-function removeEmptyStagingDirectoryWithRetry(directory) {

-      fs.rmdirSync(directory);
-      return;
-    } catch (error) {
-      failure = error;
-      // SMB can acknowledge the last file removal before the directory view
-      // catches up. Retrying an empty-directory removal is claimant-safe: any
-      // real entry keeps returning ENOTEMPTY and is never removed recursively.
-      if (error?.code !== 'ENOTEMPTY' || attempt === stagingRemovalAttempts - 1) break;
-      Atomics.wait(
-        stagingRemovalSignal,
-        0,
-        0,
-        Math.min(5 * (2 ** attempt), 250),
-      );
-    }
-  }
-  throw failure;
-}

-function stagingDirectoryAppearsEmpty(directory) {
-  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < stagingRemovalAttempts; attempt += 1) {
-    try {
-      if (fs.readdirSync(directory).length === 0) return true;
-    } catch {
-      return false;
-    }
-    if (attempt === stagingRemovalAttempts - 1) break;
-    Atomics.wait(
-      stagingRemovalSignal,
-      0,
-      0,
-      Math.min(5 * (2 ** attempt), 250),
-    );
-  }
-  return false;
-}

-function removeOwnedEmptyStagingDirectory(directory, identity, { throwOnFailure = false } = {}) {
-  let current;
-  try {
-    current = fs.lstatSync(directory, { bigint: true });
-  } catch (error) {
-    if (error?.code === 'ENOENT' || error?.code === 'ENOTDIR') return false;
-    throw error;
-  }
-  if (!current.isDirectory()
-    || current.isSymbolicLink()
-    || current.ino === 0n
-    || current.dev !== identity.device
-    || current.ino !== identity.inode) return false;
-  if (!stagingDirectoryAppearsEmpty(directory)) return false;

-  if (!quarantine) return false;

-    fs.renameSync(directory, movedPath);

-    if (throwOnFailure) throw error;
-    return false;
-  }

-  try {
-    moved = fs.lstatSync(movedPath, { bigint: true });
-  } catch {
-    return false;
-  }
-  if (!moved.isDirectory()
-    || moved.isSymbolicLink()
-    || moved.ino === 0n
-    || moved.dev !== identity.device
-    || moved.ino !== identity.inode) {

-    // quarantine name; directories have no portable no-clobber restore link.
-    return false;

-    // The unpredictable 0700 quarantine closes the public replacement race.
-    // Never recurse: unexpected contents remain available for recovery.
-    removeEmptyStagingDirectoryWithRetry(movedPath);

-  } catch (error) {
-    if (throwOnFailure) throw error;
-    return false;

-function releaseOwnedStagingBindings(registry, fileBindingRuntime) {

-  if (typeof releaseRegularFileBinding !== 'function') return;
-  for (const entry of registry) releaseRegularFileBinding(entry.binding);
-  registry.length = 0;
-}

-function artifactIdentity(artifact) {
-  return { sha256: createHash('sha256').update(artifact).digest('hex'), bytes: artifact.byteLength };

-// Locale warnings for a successfully rendered candidate. Diagnostic renderers
-// record them without printing text; validate/deliver disclose them before
-// checking the artifact and reuse the same diagnostics in successful receipts.

-  let meta;
-  try {
-    meta = JSON.parse(String(specification)).meta;
-  } catch {
-    return [];

-  if (!meta?.locale) return [];
-  const { localeDiagnostics } = await import('../renderers/shared/i18n.mjs');
-  return localeDiagnostics(type, meta);

-function deliverySuccessProvenance(receipt) {
-  return {
-    schemaVersion: 1,
-    receiptId: receipt.receiptId,
-    status: 'current',
-    command: 'deliver',
-    type: receipt.type,
-    input: receipt.input,
-    output: receipt.output,
-    specification: receipt.specification,
-    artifact: receipt.artifact,
-    ...(receipt.explainer ? { explainer: receipt.explainer } : {}),
-  };

-function inspectDeliveryProvenance(artifactPath, artifact, {
-  requireProvenance = false,
-  pathIdentityRuntime,
-  expectedSidecar,
-  inspection,
-} = {}) {
-  let sidecar = deliveryProvenancePath(artifactPath);
-  const rawHeadSidecar = rawHeadDeliveryProvenancePath(artifactPath);
-  const pending = deliveryPendingPath(artifactPath);
-  const rawHeadPending = rawHeadDeliveryPendingPath(artifactPath);
-  const legacyExtensionPending = legacyExtensionDeliverySidecarPath(
-    artifactPath,
-    '.delivery-pending.json',
-  );
-  const legacyExtensionSidecar = legacyExtensionDeliverySidecarPath(
-    artifactPath,
-    '.delivery.json',
-  );
-  const stableOutput = canonicalExistingDeliveryOutput(artifactPath);
-  const locks = [
-    deliveryLockPath(stableOutput),
-    ...legacyDeliveryLockPaths([artifactPath, stableOutput]),
-  ];
-  let foundPending;
-  try {
-    for (const candidate of [...new Set([
-      pending,
-      rawHeadPending,
-      legacyExtensionPending,
-    ].filter(Boolean))]) {
-      if (pathEntryExists(candidate)) {
-        foundPending = candidate;
-        break;
-      }
-    }
-    if (foundPending) {
-      return {
-        ok: false, status: 'failed',
-        diagnostics: [diagnostic({
-          code: 'delivery/provenance-failed',
-          message: 'A delivery attempt is unfinished or failed; complete a successful deliver before trusting this artifact.',
-          subject: { artifact: path.resolve(artifactPath), provenance: sidecar },
-          evidence: { pendingJournal: foundPending, found: true },
-          supportedFixes: ['finish any active delivery, then rerun deliver successfully; retain the pending journal until recovery succeeds'],
-        })],
-      };
-    }
-  } catch (error) {
-    return invalidProvenance(artifactPath, foundPending || pending, error.message);
-  }
-  for (const lock of locks) {
-    try {
-      if (pathEntryExists(lock)) {
-        return {
-          ok: false, status: 'locked',
-          diagnostics: [diagnostic({
-            code: 'delivery/provenance-locked',
-            message: 'Delivery ownership is unresolved while the output lock remains; complete or recover delivery before trusting this artifact.',
-            subject: { artifact: path.resolve(artifactPath), lock },
-            evidence: { deliveryLock: lock, found: true },
-            supportedFixes: ['finish the active delivery or inspect and recover the preserved lock, then rerun deliver successfully'],
-          })],
-        };
-      }
-    } catch (error) {
-      return invalidProvenance(artifactPath, lock, error.message);
-    }
-  }
-  let found;
-  try {
-    found = pathEntryExists(sidecar);
-  } catch (error) {
-    return invalidProvenance(artifactPath, sidecar, error.message);
-  }
-  if (!found && rawHeadSidecar) {
-    try {
-      found = pathEntryExists(rawHeadSidecar);
-      if (found) sidecar = rawHeadSidecar;
-    } catch (error) {
-      return invalidProvenance(artifactPath, rawHeadSidecar, error.message);
-    }
-  }
-  if (!found && legacyExtensionSidecar) {
-    try {
-      found = pathEntryExists(legacyExtensionSidecar);
-      if (found) sidecar = legacyExtensionSidecar;
-    } catch (error) {
-      return invalidProvenance(artifactPath, legacyExtensionSidecar, error.message);
-    }
-  }

-    if (!requireProvenance) return { ok: true, status: 'unknown' };
